chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Muhammad al-Wasiti, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, my father Ibrahim (peace be upon him) asked his Lord to grant him a daughter who would weep over him and lament him after his passing.

key_terms.تَنْدُبُهُ: to lament/eulogize — nadaba refers to formal mourning recitation and elegy poetry, a significant practice in Shia tradition
key_terms.يَرْزُقَهُ ابْنَةً: to grant him a daughter — rızq (divinely-bestowed provision) applied to offspring, indicating a daughter is a blessing from God

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Musa al-Kadhim ask Allah for a daughter who would mourn him after death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that his father, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) — referred to here as 'Abu Ibrahim' after his son Ibrahim — made a supplication to Allah to be blessed with a daughter who would mourn and recite elegies for him after his death. This hadith is preserved in Al-Kafi's chapter on the merits of daughters, situating the spiritual significance of daughters within the Imam's own life. Shia tradition understands this supplication as being fulfilled through the birth of Fatima al-Ma'sumah (AS), whose deep grief over her brother's imprisonment and her father's tribulations became a model of mourning.
